subject: physics
question_text: State the relation between the kinetic energy and momentum of a body.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The substitution
lines: From the second, v = p/m. Putting that
steps.margin_note: Show the substitution. The relation is worth little without the line that produces it.
steps.why: Both quantities are built from m and v, so either one can be written in terms of the other. This is only algebra.
common_mistakes: Writing the final relation with no working, which earns half the marks.

recall.must_convey: That v = p/m is substituted into KE = ½mv².
accept: KE is half m v squared and p is m v
substitute v equals p by m
v ni p by m ga rasi substitute cheyyali
reject: KE equals p squared by two m

steps.memory_tip: Both are built from m and v: write KE = ½mv² and p = mv, then remove v.

steps.label: The relation
steps.margin_note: Give the rearranged form too. Questions ask for it in both directions.
steps.why: At the same momentum a lighter body carries MORE kinetic energy — which is why a bullet, not the rifle, does the damage.

accept: KE equals p squared by two m
p equals root of two m KE
reject: substitute v equals p by m

steps.memory_tip: KE = p²/2m. Same momentum, smaller mass → larger kinetic energy.

insider_note: Asked in AP March 2026, question 14. One of the two marks is for the substitution line, so a page with only KE = p²/2m on it collects one.
